layout.description: Real run, recorded on Nov 2, 2026 with Claude Code 2.1.309 (model claude-haiku-5-5). Same edit to app.js, every run twice: without a hook the file stayed unformatted. With a PostToolUse hook (matcher Edit|Write), a small sample formatter ran after every edit, and Claude noticed it when it read the file again.
layout.companion_text: Base command per run: claude -p "<Prompt>" --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --tools Read,Edit,Write. Hook in .claude/settings.json: PostToolUse, matcher Edit|Write, node .claude/hooks/format.js. The sample formatter turns double quotes into single quotes and adds a header line. Source: Claude Code docs, Hooks, retrieved Nov 2, 2026. Paths shortened in the frame (test folder = .). Behaviour can change with version and model. Not an official Anthropic channel.

beats.spoken: Can Claude Code format your code automatically after every edit, without you having to remember to ask for it? Two real runs, one small change.
The test folder holds app.js with double quotes. Next to it sits a small sample formatter, not Prettier: it turns double quotes into single quotes and adds a header line at the top.
The hook lives in settings.json: event PostToolUse, matcher Edit or Write. So it runs after every file change Claude makes, and Claude does not have to call it.

data.quote: … with an Edit|Write matcher, so it runs only after file-editing tools.
data.translation: Runs only after tools that change files.

beats.spoken: Run one, no hook. Claude read app.js, added the function double and exported it. It said it ran nothing, since the change was simple. The double quotes stayed.
Run two, with the hook. Same edit. Then Claude read the file again and noticed on its own that a hook had reformatted it. Claude never called the hook, it ran by itself.
This is app.js after run two: a header line at the top and single quotes, without Claude having to do anything for it.
Both runs ran twice, with the same result. The hook ran after the edit every time. In real projects, according to the docs, that is where a formatter like Prettier goes.
